title: Kite spots — Belize to Costa Rica
subtitle: ranked for Oct 27 – Nov 15, 2026 and for the year · five countries · odds are estimates from published season data, not forecasts · 2026-09-05
method: Five criteria, in order: (1) wind probability inside the window, from each spot’s published season and monthly averages; (2) water and launch — flat, shallow, onshore scores above gusty, boat-start or offshore; (3) a school or rental on site, because the plan is harness-and-bar only; (4) access from the route in hours and transfers; (5) fit with the 12:00–20:00 work block, so afternoon-only thermals lose points. Odds bands: high ≥70%, medium 40–70%, low 15–40%, none <15%. Late October is the tail of the wet season everywhere; the Papagayo and Caribbean trades switch on through November.

spots.wind: Papagayo trades, side-onshore into the bay. Season early Nov → end May, plus July; ~90% of days. Monthly averages: Nov 17 · Dec 22 · Jan 23 · Feb 23 · Mar 19 · Apr 17 · May 16 kn. Blows through the day, strongest midday.
spots.water: Bay with chop, sandy launches; Copal is the school beach, Papaturro flatter; strong gusts on the big days.

odds.note: you are here Nov 2–15; November is a 12 m month, rising weekly

spots.school: Several schools at Copal and Papaturro rent full kits (~$50–80 a session, ~$250–350 a week; confirm) and teach.
spots.access: 15–20 km from the Peñas Blancas border; 1 h from Liberia; 5 h from San José. From Granada it is closer by land than by air.
spots.verdict: The trip’s kite. Base here first, not last.

spots.where: Panajachel · Santa Catarina Palopó · Isla de los Gatos
spots.wind: The xocomil: a thermal that builds noon–16:00, 8–17 kn, generally south; dry season Nov–Apr, and one operator rates Oct–Dec best. Can raise 1–2 m chop.
spots.water: Deep caldera lake, boat starts with the school, cold-ish fresh water, wind lines with holes.

odds.note: in season on your dates, but it blows 12–16 — inside the work block

spots.school: Kite School Guatemala and iKiteGt run lessons on Atitlán (and Amatitlán); rentals through them, boat included.
spots.access: 3 h shuttle from Antigua. Not on the Plan C route; the Plan B alternate day.
spots.verdict: A Plan B day, not a Plan C stop. Beautiful, light, afternoon-only.

spots.wind: NE trades across the lake, windy Nov → end Jul, 15–25 kn; best Dec–Mar and mid-Jun–Jul. Steady rather than gusty on the beach.
spots.water: Sandy beach, shallow fresh water, onshore, volcano backdrop. The friendliest launch in Nicaragua.

odds.note: the season opens in November; Nov 1 is week one

spots.school: Two schools: Ometepe Kite Center and Kitesurf Ometepe (private lessons, rental).
spots.access: Granada → San Jorge 1 h, ferry 1 h, then 40 min to Santo Domingo. San Jorge is on the road to the Costa Rica border.
spots.verdict: Nicaragua’s reliable kite. Costs a ferry day; pays it back on the way to the border.

spots.where: west shore south of the city, near the isletas
spots.wind: Same NE trades, 15–23 kn average when on, gusty, max ~34 kn; season Nov–Apr, best Dec–Mar. Year-round direction NE.
spots.water: Brown fresh water, chop, onshore on the west shore; launches are informal.

odds.note: first Papagayo days of the season; a coin flip each morning

spots.school: kitesurfnicaragua.org runs lake lessons from Granada or Ometepe in the wet season; no Granada-based rental verified — confirm before counting on it.
spots.access: Walkable from town. Zero transit cost, which is why it is in Plan C.
spots.verdict: Worth a morning if a rental exists; otherwise a run on the malecón.

spots.wind: Windy season Nov → end Jul; Nov–Feb 15–25 kn (N turning NE in Jan); Mar–May 12–20; Jun–Sep 10–18; a lull in May.
spots.water: Warm Caribbean water, reef, the east beach launch by the school.

odds.note: wind is likely; the island is two days away

spots.school: kitesurfnicaragua.org and Wingsurf Corn Islands, kite and wing, on the east beach.
spots.access: Managua → Big Corn by La Costeña ~1.5 h, then a 30-min panga. Not reachable inside this window.
spots.verdict: A separate trip. The best Caribbean kite in Nicaragua.

spots.where: the Split and the lee shore
spots.wind: Steady 12–20 kn Feb–Jul, best Feb and Jun; Dec–Jun averages 15–18 kn, 20+ in the mornings; summer 10–16. The country-wide dry season is Nov–Apr, but the caye’s own reliable window starts in February.
spots.water: Shallow, flat, turquoise water straight off the island inside the barrier reef — the best water on this list.

odds.note: late October is the wet-season tail; light unless a front pushes through

spots.school: A kite school on the island (Kitexplorer) and Velento rentals; low-season hours to confirm.
spots.verdict: A swim with a kite bag nearby. If it blows, the school is a two-minute walk.

spots.wind: Dry-season high-wind lake: Dec → May, 20–30 kn side-onshore, gusty off the hills.
spots.water: Fresh water, chop, some swell on the big days; mountain gusts.

odds.note: November is the shoulder; the main operator opens for the dry season — confirm the date

spots.school: Tico Wind runs the windsurf/kite center in season.
spots.access: 3 h from Liberia, 3.5 h from San José; on the way from Guanacaste to the volcano.
spots.verdict: December’s spot. Pass through Nov 8–12 only if Salinas is already delivering.

spots.wind: E trades 15–30 kn daily Feb → end Aug; Apr–May strongest (30+ days), Jun–Aug the most consistent (25+ days, 18–25 kn). Wind switches ESE→ENE around noon and builds after 15:00.
spots.water: Roatán’s largest natural beach: sheltered water inside, waves on the reef; Pigeon Cay for advanced riders.

odds.note: off-season and the school is closed Oct–Nov

spots.school: Kitesurf Roatán: beach assistants and a rescue boat, open December → September.
spots.access: A flight from San Pedro Sula; not on the route.
spots.verdict: Honduras’ best kite, in a month it does not blow. Not this trip.

spots.where: Chepes Beach · Little Bight · Rocky Point
spots.wind: E trades Dec → Apr; shallow sheltered turquoise water.
spots.water: Sheltered lagoon, sandy; small island, small scene.
spots.school: Kitesurf & Flyboard Utila; a Facebook-scale operation — confirm it is active.
spots.access: Ferry from La Ceiba or flight from SAP; not on the route.
spots.verdict: Diving island that also kites. Not this trip.

spots.where: inside the reef, north of town
spots.wind: Season Jan → Apr with the dry-season trades.
spots.water: Reef-protected flat water; busier than Caye Caulker.
spots.school: Shops and instructors in San Pedro.
spots.access: Water taxi from Belize City; Caye Caulker is the better base for the same water.
spots.verdict: Skip; Caye Caulker has the same lagoon with less town.

spots.wind: Apr–May the best months for wind sports on this coast; dry-season trades Nov–Apr at 15–25 kn on paper.
spots.water: Long sandy peninsula, open water, less reef shelter than the cayes.
spots.school: Placencia has the mainland’s kite operators; seasonal.
spots.access: A day’s bus from Belize City or the Placencia water taxi.

spots.wind: Light, stable thermal; used by the Guatemala school for teaching.
spots.water: Warm crater lake; heavily polluted — the reason it is a lesson venue, not a destination.

odds.note: close to the airport, light wind, dirty water

spots.school: Kite School Guatemala teaches here as well as on Atitlán.
spots.verdict: Only if a rested afternoon appears between the flight and Antigua. Unlikely.

spots.wind: The Papagayo blows offshore here, which is what makes the surf glassy; kiting exists at Guasacate and Astillero on side-shore days in season.
spots.water: Surf beaches; offshore wind means a kite goes to sea.

odds.note: a surf spot with a kite footnote

spots.school: Surf camps; no dedicated kite school verified.
spots.verdict: Bring the surfboard, not the kite.

countries.call: The only high-odds wind in the window. Bahía Salinas opens in early November at ~17 kn averages and climbs to 22–23 by December; Lake Arenal follows from December. You land in the country on Nov 2 and stay to Nov 15 — that is the trip’s kite block, and the reason to arrive at Salinas rather than San José.

Season opens the week you are there. Ometepe’s Santo Domingo is the reliable, schooled, sandy option; Granada’s lakeshore is the zero-transit option with no verified rental. Little Corn is the best Caribbean wind in the country and two days out of reach.
One real spot, Lake Atitlán, thermal and afternoon-only, in season on your dates. It costs three hours off the route and the middle of the work block. A Plan B day.
The best flat water on the list and the wrong month. Caye Caulker’s own window is February to July. Swim, snorkel, run the island; kite if a front arrives.
Camp Bay on Roatán is the region’s second-best spot for the year and blows February to August; the school is closed in October and November. Copán, where the route actually goes, has no wind at all.

route: Re-derive the Nov 2 leg: Bahía Salinas is 15–20 km from the Peñas Blancas border. Granada → Rivas → border → La Cruz is 3–4 h by road with the crossing; the MGA → SJO flight ($120–250) lands you five hours from the wind. Go by land, arrive at Playa Copal by early afternoon Nov 2, and let San José wait. Border 06:00–22:00 (Sundays to 20:00); Nov 2 is a Monday.

If Nicaragua kiting matters, swap the second Granada night for Ometepe: Granada Oct 31 → San Jorge ferry Nov 1 → Santo Domingo (two schools, sandy launch) → back to San Jorge Nov 2, which is already on the road to the border. Odds rise from ~40% to ~50% and the launch is far safer; the cost is one ferry and a 40-min road, ~$25–40.
Belize stays a swim. Keep the Caye Caulker morning as snorkel and run; check the school on arrival and ride only if the trades show.

Guatemala: Atitlán only in Plan B, and only by moving that day’s work block to 16:00–24:00 or accepting a dead block. Not worth it against a Copán morning unless the forecast the week before shows 15+ kn.

Gear: harness, bar, and a leash. Rent at Copal or Papaturro for the fortnight (a weekly rate beats sessions after day four); rent on Ometepe by the hour. Leave the quiver; four flights, three of them Cessnas.
Pre-register the forecast: 70% that Salinas delivers a ridable day within the first three days (Nov 2–4); 40% that Granada does on Nov 1; 20% that Caye Caulker does on Oct 31. Score them on arrival.
verify: A Granada-based kite rental in early November — none verified; the lake school operates from Granada or Ometepe on request.
